summary: Narrow UI accessibility retest after aside sticky removal + scroll-mt-24 on contact form. Verified on desktop 1920x800 and mobile 390x844: load-sample-button loads 5-chapter sample, request-proposal-button is clickable via ordinary Playwright native .click() (no force, no dispatch), contact form opens with name input focused, header renders below fixed nav (form top y ~96px, > nav height), and name/email/submit are reachable via ordinary scroll_into_view_if_needed + native click. No DB modifications performed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Aside is now non-sticky (space-y-5 only) and contact form has scroll-mt-24. Native Playwright clicks work on request-proposal-button on both desktop and mobile; no synthetic dispatch needed. Contact form header y ~96px (below fixed nav ~64-88px). Name input is autofocused. All target testids present: load-sample-button, request-proposal-button, proposal-contact-form, contact-name-input, contact-email-input, submit-booking-button.
rca of the issue: Prior iteration3 issue: sticky aside was tall enough to intercept native clicks in some scroll positions. Root cause: sticky positioning of the aside on the proposal builder page made the request-proposal-button viewport-overlap fragile. Mitigation applied by main agent: removed sticky positioning entirely (aside className reduced to space-y-5). Verified fix: native page.click on request-proposal-button now succeeds on both 1920x800 and 390x844 viewports without force=True/dispatchEvent. Also added scroll-mt-24 to contact form so header lands below fixed nav after focus-scroll.
